record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: For sufficiently chaotic billiard models with a small hole H of relative size h and escape rate γ, can one prove a local escape-rate formula analogous to the known formulas for piecewise expanding maps, in which γ/h has a limit as the hole shrinks to a point and the limiting value reflects whether the limiting point is periodic and the stability of that periodic point?

evidence.quote: In [18, 47] it is shown that γ/h can reach a limit, the local escape rate, as the hole shrinks to a point, and that the limit depends on whether the point is periodic.
Open problem 2. Local escape rate: Proof of a formula similar to Eq. (7) for sufficiently chaotic billiard models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T:M\to M$ be a sufficiently chaotic billiard map (for example, a finite-horizon dispersing Sinai billiard or a Bunimovich-type hyperbolic billiard) preserving a smooth invariant probability measure $\mu$. For a measurable subset $H\subset M$ (the "hole"), define the open system by removing trajectories that enter $H$, and let
$$\gamma(H)=-\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log\mu\{x\in M : T^k(x)\notin H\text{ for all }0\le k\le n\}$$
denote the escape rate (assumed to exist). Let $h=\mu(H)$ denote the relative size of the hole, and let $\{H_\varepsilon\}_{\varepsilon>0}$ be a family of holes shrinking to a point $z\in M$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$, with $h_\varepsilon=\mu(H_\varepsilon)\to 0$.

Prove that the local escape rate
$$\rho(z)=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\frac{\gamma(H_\varepsilon)}{h_\varepsilon}$$
exists, and establish an explicit formula for $\rho(z)$ of the type known for piecewise expanding maps: namely,
- if $z$ is not a periodic point of $T$, then $\rho(z)=1$;
- if $z$ is periodic of prime period $p$, then 
$$\rho(z)=1-\frac{1}{|\det DT^p(z)|_u|},$$
where $|\det DT^p(z)|_u|$ denotes the unstable Jacobian (product of unstable eigenvalues) of $DT^p$ at $z$, so that the limit reflects both the periodicity and the hyperbolic stability of $z$.
artifact.status_search_result: Local escape-rate formulas of the desired type are established for piecewise expanding maps and certain hyperbolic systems via Keller–Liverani perturbation theory (Keller–Liverani, Ferguson–Pollicott, etc.). For genuinely chaotic billiards (e.g., Sinai dispersing billiards), existence of an escape rate and conditionally invariant measures has been proved (Demers–Wright–Young, Demers–Zhang, and recent projective-cone work by Demers–Korepanov–Liverani), but a fully general local-escape-rate formula distinguishing periodic vs. non-periodic limit points and involving the unstable Jacobian has not, to current knowledge, been proved for chaotic billiards; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Escape Rates and Physically Relevant Measures for Billiards with Small Holes
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of a common escape rate and limiting conditionally invariant distribution for dispersing billiards with small holes.
status_evidence.claim: Escape rates exist for dispersing billiards with small holes, but a local escape-rate formula at a point is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Rare Events, Escape Rates and Quasistationarity: Some Exact Formulae
status_evidence.snippet: Keller–Liverani exact formulae for escape rates relating γ/μ(H) to periodicity and derivatives for piecewise expanding maps.
status_evidence.claim: The desired local escape-rate formula is known for piecewise expanding maps, motivating the open problem for billiards.

status_evidence.title: Projective Cones for Sequential Dispersing Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Birkhoff cone constructions for transfer operators on dispersing billiards, applied to open billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances address escape-related spectral problems for billiards but stop short of proving the local escape-rate formula.

status_evidence.title: Dispersing Billiards with Small Holes
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open dispersing billiards; discusses escape rates and outstanding questions.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates local escape rate at periodic points for billiards remains a problem requiring further development.
